preStudy.title: Prerequisites & Diagnostic Review
preStudy.subtitle: Review foundational concepts required before studying polygon similarity: ratios, sum of quadrilateral angles, and quadrilateral properties.

cards.title: Ratio & Proportionality
cards.desc: A ratio compares two quantities $\frac{a}{b}$. Two ratios are equal $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d} = k$ if they simplify to the same constant factor $k$. Cross-multiplication yields $a \times d = b \times c$.

cards.title: Quadrilateral Angle Sum
cards.desc: The sum of the measures of the interior angles of any convex quadrilateral is always $360^\circ$. If 3 angles are known, the 4th is: $m(\angle 4) = 360^\circ - (\angle_1 + \angle_2 + \angle_3)$.

cards.title: Special Quadrilateral Properties
cards.desc: In a parallelogram/rhombus: opposite angles are equal ($m(\angle A) = m(\angle C)$), and consecutive angles are supplementary ($m(\angle A) + m(\angle B) = 180^\circ$). In rectangles and squares, all 4 angles are $90^\circ$.

diagnosticQuestions.text: 1. In any quadrilateral $ABCD$, if $m(\angle A) = 90^\circ$, $m(\angle B) = 120^\circ$, and $m(\angle C) = 45^\circ$, what is $m(\angle D)$?
diagnosticQuestions.explanation: The sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral is $360^\circ$. Thus: $m(\angle D) = 360^\circ - (90^\circ + 120^\circ + 45^\circ) = 360^\circ - 255^\circ = 105^\circ$.

realWorldApps.solutionHtml:
Geometric Aspect Ratio Proof:
1. Cinema Screen:
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{\text{Width}}{\text{Height}} = \frac{45}{25} = \frac{9}{5} = 1.80$$ 2. TV Screen 1 (36 in × 27 in):
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{36}{27} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$$ Since $\frac{4}{3} \ne \frac{9}{5}$, TV 1 is NOT similar to the cinema screen. The scene will either be clipped at the sides or shown with letterbox bars.
3. TV Screen 2 (36 in × 20 in):
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{36}{20} = \frac{9}{5} = 1.80$$ Since the ratio of dimensions is identical ($\frac{36}{45} = \frac{20}{25} = \frac{4}{5}$), TV 2 is geometrically similar to the cinema screen.
Conclusion: TV 2 displays the movie with complete fidelity and zero image distortion.

realWorldApps.solutionHtml:
Step-by-Step Similarity Verification:
Both shapes are rectangles, so all interior angles are equal to $90^\circ$.
Now test the proportionality of corresponding dimensions:
1. Width Ratio: $\frac{\text{Laptop Width}}{\text{Wall Width}} = \frac{13.25}{53} = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$
2. Height Ratio: $\frac{\text{Laptop Height}}{\text{Wall Height}} = \frac{10.6}{42.4} = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$
Since $\frac{13.25}{53} = \frac{10.6}{42.4} = \frac{1}{4}$, the corresponding dimensions are proportional.
Conclusion: Yes, the two shapes are similar, and the similarity ratio of the laptop screen to the projected wall image is $k = \frac{1}{4}$ (meaning the projector provides a $4\times$ magnification).

foundation.formulaText: $$\text{Polygon } ABCD \sim \text{Polygon } EFGH \iff \begin{cases} m(\angle A)=m(\angle E), \; m(\angle B)=m(\angle F), \; m(\angle C)=m(\angle G), \; m(\angle D)=m(\angle H) \\[8pt] \dfrac{AB}{EF} = \dfrac{BC}{FG} = \dfrac{CD}{GH} = \dfrac{DA}{HE} = k \end{cases}$$
foundation.formulaSubtext: Two polygons having the same number of sides are similar if and only if BOTH conditions are satisfied together: (1) Corresponding angles are equal in measure, AND (2) Corresponding side lengths are proportional.

rules.title: Two Simultaneous Conditions
rules.desc: Equality of angles alone is NOT sufficient (e.g. rectangle vs square), nor is proportionality of sides alone sufficient (e.g. rhombus vs square). Both must hold true!

rules.title: Vertex Correspondence Order
rules.desc: Vertices must be written in exact corresponding order: $ABCD \sim EFGH \implies A \leftrightarrow E, B \leftrightarrow F, C \leftrightarrow G, D \leftrightarrow H$. Side ratios follow immediately: $\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{BC}{FG} = \dots$

rules.title: Similarity Ratio / Scale Factor $k$
rules.desc: If $k > 1$, polygon 1 is an Enlargement of polygon 2. If $0 < k < 1$, it is a Reduction. If $k = 1$, the polygons are Congruent.

rules.title: Transitivity Principle
rules.desc: Two polygons similar to a third polygon are similar to each other. In addition, all congruent polygons are similar ($k = 1$), but similar polygons are NOT necessarily congruent.

Calculate the ratio of corresponding side lengths:
$$\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}, \quad \frac{BC}{FG} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}, \quad \frac{CD}{GH} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}, \quad \frac{DA}{HE} = \frac{15}{10} = \frac{3}{2}$$
Since corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio $\frac{AB}{EF} = \frac{BC}{FG} = \frac{CD}{GH} = \frac{DA}{HE} = \frac{3}{2}$, the two polygons are similar.

cards.ans: Polygon $ABCD \sim$ Polygon $EFGH$, and the similarity ratio is $k = \frac{3}{2}$ (or $1.5$).

steps.text: In trapezoid $ABCD$: Consecutive angles between parallel bases are supplementary: $m(\angle A) = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$, and $m(\angle B) = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$. In trapezoid $SPQR$: $m(\angle Q) = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$, and $m(\angle R) = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$. Thus: $m(\angle A) = m(\angle S) = 120^\circ$, $m(\angle B) = m(\angle P) = 120^\circ$, $m(\angle C) = m(\angle Q) = 60^\circ$, $m(\angle D) = m(\angle R) = 60^\circ$.

Calculate the ratios of corresponding sides:
$$\frac{AB}{SP} = \frac{3}{4.5} = \frac{30}{45} = \frac{2}{3}, \quad \frac{BC}{PQ} = \frac{5}{7.5} = \frac{50}{75} = \frac{2}{3}$$
$$\frac{CD}{QR} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}, \quad \frac{DA}{RS} = \frac{5}{7.5} = \frac{2}{3}$$
Both conditions are satisfied simultaneously with constant ratio $k = \frac{2}{3}$.

• $m(\angle C) = m(\angle G) = 135^\circ$
• $m(\angle F) = m(\angle B) = 90^\circ, m(\angle E) = m(\angle A) = 75^\circ$

2. Similarity Ratio:
$$k = \frac{CD}{GH} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{8\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$$
3. Finding Lengths:

Parallelograms Similarity Proof:
• Angle Check: In $ABCD$, consecutive angles are supplementary: $m(\angle A) = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$. Thus $m(\angle A) = m(\angle P) = 60^\circ$.

mcqs.q: In the figure: Polygon $ABCD \sim$ Polygon $EBHG$. If $DC = 6\text{ cm}$, $GH = 4\text{ cm}$, $EB = 5\text{ cm}$, and $AE = x\text{ cm}$, what is the value of $x$?
mcqs.proof: The scale factor is $\frac{CD}{HG} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5$. Since side $AB = AE + EB = x + 5$, we have $\frac{AB}{EB} = 1.5 \implies \frac{x + 5}{5} = 1.5 \implies x + 5 = 7.5 \implies x = 2.5\text{ cm}$.

mcqs.q: Two similar polygons have a ratio between two corresponding sides of $2 : 3$. If the perimeter of the smaller polygon is $34\text{ cm}$, what is the perimeter of the larger polygon?
mcqs.proof: The ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of sides: $\frac{P_{\text{small}}}{P_{\text{large}}} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{34}{P} = \frac{2}{3} \implies P = \frac{34 \times 3}{2} = 17 \times 3 = 51\text{ cm}$.

mcqs.q: Teacher asked: 'Are all regular polygons similar?' Ahmed answered: 'Yes, all regular polygons are similar.' Nourhan answered: 'No, they are only similar if they have the same number of sides.' Who is correct?
mcqs.proof: Nourhan is correct. Regular polygons can only be similar if they have the identical number of sides. An equilateral triangle (3 sides) can never be similar to a regular hexagon (6 sides) or a square (4 sides).

mcqs.q: Marwan used CAD software to scale down a rectangle of length $10\text{ cm}$ and width $4\text{ cm}$. If the width of the reduced rectangle is $3\text{ cm}$, what is its length?
mcqs.proof: By proportion of dimensions: $\frac{L}{10} = \frac{3}{4} \implies L = \frac{10 \times 3}{4} = \frac{30}{4} = 7.5\text{ cm}$.
